metadata.source: Badali et al. (2024), Figure 2 — SEG Interpretation

archetypes.label: Homoclinal Ramp
archetypes.seismic_character: low-relief clinoform packages, tabular geometry, weak amplitude contrast
archetypes.reservoir_quality: low to moderate (thin, widespread, low relief)

archetypes.label: Distally Steepened Ramp
archetypes.geometry: low-angle inner ramp, steepening distally (slope break at shelf edge)
archetypes.seismic_character: low-angle proximal clinoforms, steep distal margin, mounded geometry at slope break
archetypes.discrimination_confidence: LOW-MODERATE (distal steepening can mimic volcanic intrusion or mud volcano)
archetypes.mud_volcano_risk: HIGH (steepened margin can look like mud volcano cone)

archetypes.label: Non-Rimmed Attached Platform (Shelf)
archetypes.geometry: broad flat-topped shelf, attached to hinterland, no rim barrier
archetypes.seismic_character: high-amplitude flat top, low-angle margins, sheet-like geometry, weak rim
archetypes.reservoir_quality: moderate (wide area but low relief, thin)
archetypes.discrimination_confidence: LOW (easily confused with detrital shelf, shale platform)
archetypes.sabah_relevance: Oligocene-Miocene broad shelf; Luconia-style attached platform

archetypes.label: Slightly Rimmed Platform
archetypes.geometry: flat-topped shelf with low-relief rim, marginal slope 5-15°
archetypes.seismic_character: weak rim crest amplitude, subtle slope break, internal platform reflections visible
archetypes.reservoir_quality: moderate (rim adds relief, platform interior thinner)
archetypes.discrimination_confidence: LOW (subtle rim easily missed; confused with ramp)
archetypes.sabah_relevance: transitional; early Miocene before full collision

archetypes.label: Rimmed Platform
archetypes.geometry: well-developed rim crest (reef rim), steep margin slope 30-70°, flat interior platform
archetypes.seismic_character: high-amplitude continuous rim crest, steep margin reflections, weak interior platform, possible progradation packages
archetypes.reservoir_quality: HIGH (rim = best reservoir; steep slopes = thick platform section)
archetypes.mud_volcano_risk: LOW (steep margin + high relief rim is distinctive)
archetypes.sabah_relevance: Miocene icehouse (I); highest chaseability; proven producers Tepat, Megah, Layang-Layang

archetypes.label: Isolated Platform
archetypes.geometry: isolated flat-topped carbonate build-up, surrounded by deep water, can be nonrimmed, slightly rimmed, or fully rimmed
archetypes.seismic_character: high-amplitude rim crest, steep flanks, isolated high-relief mound, onlap terminations on flanks
archetypes.reservoir_quality: HIGH (isolation = best porosity; flank = secondary reservoir)
archetypes.discrimination_confidence: HIGH (isolated high-relief mound is most distinctive carbonate structure)
archetypes.mud_volcano_risk: LOW (isolated mound in deep water is hard to confuse)
archetypes.sabah_relevance: possible in post-collision strike-slip setting; pinnacle reefs in deep water

archetypes.label: Pinnacle Reef
archetypes.geometry: small isolated mounded carbonate build-up, pointed or rounded top, no flat top, <2 km width typical
archetypes.seismic_character: small mounded high-relief reflection, pointed or rounded crest, steep flanks, isolated in deep water
archetypes.reservoir_quality: HIGH (small, dense, good porosity; flanks are reservoir)
archetypes.discrimination_confidence: MODERATE (small mounds hard to distinguish from volcanic knobs, mud volcano cones, salt diapirs)
archetypes.mud_volcano_risk: HIGH (pinnacle shape + isolated in deep water is mud volcano archetype)
archetypes.volcanic_intrusion_risk: HIGH (small volcanic intrusive domes have identical shape)
archetypes.sabah_relevance: highest false-positive risk; requires AVO + well control to confirm

Icehouse (I).resedimentation: extensive megabreccias, debris flows, periplatform ooze

Greenhouse (G).sabah_expected: Oligocene pre-collision — ramp / distally steepened ramp

step_1_climate_regime.question: What is the seismic age context?

step_2_geometry.question: What is the geometric relationship to hinterland?

attached_to_land.note: Carbonate factory connected to siliciclastic sediment source

step_3_rim.question: Is there a visible rim crest and steep margin?

step_4_slope.question: What is the margin slope angle from seismic?

step_5_features.question: What additional seismic features are present?

chaotic_surface_no_geometry.warning: Mud volcano, volcanic intrusion, or basement high

primary_play.discrimination_gap: Vp alone cannot distinguish carbonate from basement at φ<15%
primary_play.seismic_misclassification_risk: mud volcanoes + volcanic intrusions mimic carbonate mounds (internal PETRONAS study)

discrimination_workflow: Step 1: Age context from seismic stratigraphy → Icehouse vs Greenhouse
Step 2: Geometry classification → attached vs isolated, rimmed vs non-rimmed
Step 3: Slope angle from seismic → >30° = Icehouse rimmed; <15° = Greenhouse ramp
Step 4: Feature checklist → megabreccias, karst, progradation
Step 5: Vp-porosity from well control or rock physics model
Step 6: AVO analysis to rule out mud volcano / volcanic intrusion
Step 7: Assign archetype + confidence; if confidence < 0.7 → exploratory
